sections.h2: Where is Troup County and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Troup County sits on Georgia's western edge against the Alabama line, with LaGrange as county seat and largest city. The county covers 446 square miles, of which 414 are land, and it lies in the Piedmont. Interstate 85 and Interstate 185 cross it, along with U.S. 27 and several state routes, so Atlanta commuters and Columbus-area workers both live here.

The Georgia General Assembly drew the county's boundaries on June 9, 1826, after the Creek ceded the land in the 1825 Treaty of Indian Springs, according to Wikipedia's county entry. Cotton mills built around LaGrange in the late 1800s anchored the local economy for decades. Textile work later moved overseas, and auto parts suppliers serving the nearby Kia plant now fill part of that gap. West Point Lake and Callaway Gardens bring in visitors.

Three cities sit inside the county: LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point. Long Cane, Mountville, Harrisonville and Abbottsford are unincorporated communities. A house in LaGrange, a lake-area lot near West Point and a farm parcel outside Hogansville each draw a different buyer, which matters when you decide how to sell with a tax bill still open.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Troup County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 72,844 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 4.9% from the 2020 base. Homeownership runs at 60.6% for 2020 to 2024, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $217,200.

About four in ten households rent, and 88.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. That stability means long-held homes, inherited houses and rentals make up much of what changes hands. Residents 65 or older make up 17.8% of the county, so estate sales are a regular part of the market.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Troup County?
sections.html:
Two offices handle your tax, and neither controls the other. The tax commissioner bills and collects; the Board of Tax Assessors, working through the Property Appraisal Department, sets value.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 883-1620, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with bills, payments, mobile home and timber tax, and tags.
  • Property Appraisal: (706) 883-1625, at 100 Ridley Avenue, Suite 2100, LaGrange, for values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens.

The county's appraisal FAQ says the assessors are a part-time citizens board, so a phone call may reach voicemail. The Chief Appraiser is chosen by that board, and the board answers to state law, not to the county commission, which only controls its budget. Payments can be made on the county's online payment page, which lists a Property Taxes option, or by calling the tax office.

sections.h2: When are Troup County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The county's property tax page gives November 15 as the official deadline, and penalties and interest accrue afterward. Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that counties may move the statewide default date, so the date printed on your bill is the one that counts.

Value is fixed as of January 1, and the taxable amount is 40% of fair market value. The millage rate comes from the school board, the county governing authority and any other taxing body covering your parcel. The county's own illustration uses a rate of .030260 and says exemptions are subtracted first. Mobile home owners and timber sellers deal with the same tax commissioner, on separate schedules.

  • Assessed value is 40% of market value under state law.
  • One mill equals $1.00 per $1,000 of assessed value.
  • A change in assessed value or a lost exemption can raise a bill even when the rate holds still.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Troup County valuation?
sections.html:
Appeals start with the annual assessment notice, and you get 45 days from the date printed on it. Miss that window and the right to appeal that year's value is lost.

The county invites sales data, photographs of similar recently sold homes, or anything else you want the appraisers to weigh. If you stay in the process, the Board of Equalization is the usual next stop. Grand jury members appoint it, fellow property owners sit on it, and it costs nothing. Arbitration is the alternative: each side picks and pays an arbitrator and splits the cost of a third. A Superior Court appeal carries a $25.00 filing fee, according to the county FAQ.

After a board or court result, state law bars the assessors from changing that value for two years unless they inspect the property on site.

sections.h2: Which Troup County exemptions are worth a look?
sections.html:
Homestead exemption applications are accepted from January 1 through April 1 each year, per the county, and missing the window waives the exemption for that year. Call Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625 for the forms and the amounts that apply.

Other special exemptions are kept on file at the same office. Georgia's county facts page adds that a returned property keeps its prior-year value if you skip filing a new return, and that freeport inventory exemptions are a local vote. Moving to a new house means a new homestead application at the new address.

  • Own and live in the house on January 1 to qualify.
  • File by April 1 for the current tax year.
  • Refund claims for taxes wrongly assessed must start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Troup County house?
sections.html:
Ask the tax commissioner for a payoff before you set a closing date, and have the closing agent pay it from your proceeds. The bill follows the owner of record on January 1, so a sale in the fall can leave you holding a bill for a house you no longer own unless the settlement statement splits it.

The tax commissioner's news page posts a courtesy list for tax sales and notes that excess funds from a sale are paid only to the record owner at the time of the sale or to other lienholders. A house that sat unpaid for several years, whether rental, inheritance or vacancy, can carry more than one year of bills, so ask for each year in writing.

Cash buyers can close with an unpaid bill on the table, since the payout comes out of the sale. Compare the closing statement against the payoff letter before you sign.

faqs.q: What number do I call about a Troup County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call (706) 883-1620 for the tax commissioner. Value and exemption questions go to Property Appraisal at (706) 883-1625.

faqs.q: Is November 15 the deadline in Troup County?
faqs.a: Yes, the county's tax page calls November 15 the official deadline for property taxes. Penalties and interest accrue after it, so check the date on your own bill.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a Troup County appeal?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the annual assessment notice. Appeals only follow a notice, and a missed deadline ends the right to appeal that year.

faqs.q: When can I apply for a homestead exemption in Troup County?
faqs.a: Applications are accepted between January 1 and April 1. Filing after April 1 means no exemption for that year.

faqs.q: Who pays the bill if I sell during the year?
faqs.a: The owner of record on January 1 is billed. Settle it at closing and ask the tax commissioner for a payoff letter beforehand.
